about.title: About Global City Review
about.p1: Global City Review is an international commentary site for urban policy researchers, public-sector teams, consultancies, media editors and long-horizon city watchers. We cover urban governance, infrastructure, regional economics, public finance, housing and population movement, with an emphasis on structural change visible in public records rather than short-lived rankings or project publicity.
about.p2: The site is maintained by the editorial team of the Global Urban Policy Institute. We publish editorials, city analysis, regional outlooks, expert perspectives and report-style commentary. Each piece should identify its evidence, public sources, inference boundaries and uncertainties. The material is for discussion of public issues and does not constitute legal, investment, procurement, planning approval or business advice.

principles.title: Editorial Principles
principles.h1: Arguments may be clear; evidence must be traceable
principles.p1: We welcome judgment in urban commentary, but we do not package speculation as fact. Claims involving policy, investment, population, transport, public services or municipal finance should rely on official documents, regulatory notices, original statistics, academic material or credible reporting whenever possible.
principles.p2: We do not fabricate expert interviews, conference remarks, internal documents or unpublished data. When an article uses editorial analysis, it must distinguish fact, inference and commentary; for contested policy or commercial implications, it should describe alternative explanations and downside risks.
principles.p3: We prioritize issues that shape long-term urban capability: fiscal resilience, housing affordability, infrastructure governance, regional coordination, industrial geography, public trust and climate adaptation. Judgments about cities or regions should avoid simplistic labels and show the relationship between institutions, resources and time horizons.
principles.p4: Readers can contact the editorial desk through the footer email if they find a factual error, broken source or unclear boundary between fact and opinion. We check original sources first and, when needed, update, annotate or correct the article. Corrections are not used to silently change a central argument.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.p1: Global City Review follows a data-minimization approach. When you visit the site, servers, hosting providers or security services may record IP address, browser type, access time, request path, error logs and basic device information for page delivery, security, performance investigation and abnormal-request detection.
privacy.p2: The site currently does not offer reader accounts or audience-profiling tools, and it does not collect reader email addresses through forms. We receive an email address, message body and attachments only when a reader actively writes to the contact email shown in the footer.
privacy.p3: Reader messages may include story suggestions, factual corrections, source additions, licensing questions or cooperation inquiries. We use this information only for editorial verification, replies, compliance retention and security auditing. We do not sell, rent or use it for advertising targeting.
privacy.p4: To query, correct or delete email records related to you, contact

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.p1: The content on this site is for discussion of urban policy, regional development and public issues. Analysis and judgments are based on public materials and editorial interpretation; they do not constitute legal, investment, procurement, planning approval, policy implementation or business decision-making advice.
terms.p2: Readers may quote article titles, short excerpts and links within reasonable limits while preserving attribution. Republishing full articles, systematically scraping pages, turning commentary into commercial reports or training material, or reusing content in a misleading context requires prior written permission.
terms.p3: External links identify public sources or reference materials. Global City Review does not control external sites, their later changes, availability or data accuracy. If a source link stops working, readers may contact the editorial desk for verification support.
terms.p4: For licensing, factual corrections, source additions or cooperation, contact

cookie.title: Cookie Policy
cookie.p1: Global City Review currently does not use advertising-tracking cookies, cross-site marketing tags or cookie-based reader profiling.
cookie.p2: Hosting, content delivery, security protection or framework operation may use necessary cookies or similar technologies for language routing, session safety, load balancing, cache control and abnormal-request detection. These technologies support availability and security only.
cookie.p3: If we later add analytics, account features or other services that require additional cookies, we will update this page before activation with the purpose, retention period, third-party provider and opt-out options.
cookie.p4: Readers can delete or restrict cookies through browser settings. Restricting necessary cookies may affect language redirects, security checks or page loading behavior, but it should not affect the basic ability to read public articles.

about.title: About Global City Review
about.description: Public information about Global City Review.

sections.heading: What we cover
body: Global City Review is a city policy, infrastructure and urban affairs news service operated by Global City Review. It covers city analysis, regional outlook, expert perspectives, with emphasis on verifiable facts, clear context, and practical relevance for its readers.
The site is written for professionals, researchers, public-affairs readers, and interested general audiences who need concise orientation without exaggerated certainty.

sections.heading: How to use our work
body: Articles may summarize public documents, official notices, company announcements, research material, event information, and other accessible sources. We distinguish proposals, approvals, launches, results, and later updates so early-stage plans are not described as completed outcomes.

Readers should use the content for news reading, research, and general situational awareness. Before relying on any item for a decision, consult original documents, current dates, applicable jurisdictions, and qualified professionals.

editorial-principles.title: Editorial Principles
editorial-principles.description: Public information about Global City Review.

sections.heading: Independence and sourcing
body: Global City Review is edited to preserve independence from advertisers, sponsors, sources, and political or commercial interests. Coverage choices are based on relevance, evidence, public interest, and fit with the site’s stated beats.

We prefer primary sources, named organizations, official records, public filings, research reports, and clearly attributable statements. Unverified rumors or second-hand claims are not presented as settled fact.

sections.heading: Review, updates, and corrections
body: Editors check names, dates, figures, locations, document status, and context before publication when practical. If credible new information changes a story, we may update the article, add a correction note, or revise wording to reflect the available record.
Readers can send correction requests to {email}. We review requests against source material and may receive written notices at {address}.

sections.heading: Automation and limits
body: Editorial teams may use translation, research, summarization, formatting, or quality-control tools, including automated assistance. Human editors remain responsible for publication decisions and for ensuring tools do not invent sources, quotes, or certainty.

Content is for information only and is not legal, investment, tax, medical, engineering, procurement, or policy-compliance advice. We use cautious language where outcomes depend on regulation, markets, litigation, technical review, or future implementation.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: Public information about Global City Review.

sections.heading: Information we collect
body: When readers visit Global City Review, technical systems may collect server logs, page paths, access times, device and browser type, broad location, referring pages, IP address, cookie identifiers, and error information.

When you contact us, we process the name, email address, organization, message content, attachments, and other details you choose to provide. Search queries and forms should not include sensitive personal information.

sections.heading: How information is used
body: We use information to operate and secure the site, measure public page performance, respond to messages, process correction or privacy requests, detect abuse, and improve loading and navigation.

Hosting, analytics, security, email, translation, and content-delivery providers may process limited technical data for us. We do not sell reader personal information or add editorial contacts to unrelated marketing lists.

sections.heading: Retention, rights, and contact
body: We keep information only as long as reasonably needed for operations, security, legal obligations, dispute handling, and editorial accountability. Retention periods vary by data type and provider.
Depending on your location, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict, or object to certain processing. Requests can be sent to {email}; postal correspondence may be sent to {address}.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.description: Public information about Global City Review.

sections.heading: Permitted use
body: You may read, link to, and quote short excerpts from Global City Review for lawful personal, research, educational, or professional reference, provided attribution is clear and the context is not misleading.
You may not scrape at scale, republish full articles, remove attribution, bypass technical controls, interfere with the site, or use content in a way that violates rights, laws, or platform rules.

sections.heading: No professional advice
body: Content is provided for general information and editorial reference. It is not legal, investment, tax, medical, engineering, procurement, or policy-compliance advice, and it should not replace reviewing original documents or consulting qualified professionals.
Facts, laws, markets, standards, policies, and project details can change after publication. We do not promise that every article is complete, current, or suitable for any particular decision.

sections.heading: Copyright, links, and liability
body: Unless otherwise stated, site text, design, and original editorial materials are protected by copyright and other rights. Third-party names, logos, images, documents, and links remain the property or responsibility of their respective owners.
External links are provided for context and convenience. We are not responsible for third-party sites. Questions about these terms can be sent to {email}; notices may be mailed to {address}.

cookie-policy.title: Cookie Policy
cookie-policy.description: Public information about Global City Review.

sections.heading: Essential and preference cookies
body: Global City Review uses essential cookies and similar technologies to make pages load, remember security choices, manage language or region preferences, and support basic site functions.

Preference cookies may remember settings such as language, display options, or selected filters. Disabling them may make the site less convenient but should not prevent access to ordinary public pages.

sections.heading: Analytics and embedded services
body: Analytics cookies help us understand page traffic, device categories, referrers, errors, and content performance in aggregated or limited form. These signals support editorial planning and technical maintenance.
Embedded services, such as video, maps, social sharing, fonts, analytics, or security tools, may place their own cookies or collect technical data under their own policies.

sections.heading: Managing cookies
body: You can control cookies through browser settings, device controls, private browsing modes, consent tools where available, or third-party opt-out mechanisms. Blocking some cookies may affect preferences, embedded media, analytics, or security checks.
For questions about cookies or related privacy choices, contact {email}. Written requests may also be sent to {address}.
